question: George can do 35% of the total work in 6 days. Jim and George together completed a piece of work in 12 days. In how many days could Jim, working alone, complete the entire task?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**George** completes 100% work in 6 × (100 / 35) = 120/7 days.

Total Work (LCM of 120/7 and 12) = 120 units.

Efficiency of **George** = 7 and Efficiency of (**Jim** + **George**) = 10.

Efficiency of **Jim** = 10 − 7 = 3 units/day.

Time taken by **Jim** = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Work done by **George** = 35% in 6 days.

Time taken by **Jim** and **George** together = 12 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken by **George** to complete 100% work = 6 ÷ 0.35 = 600/35 = 120/7 days.

⇒ Let the total work be the **LCM** of 120/7 and 12, which is 120 units.

⇒ Efficiency of **Jim** = Efficiency of (**Jim** + **George**) − Efficiency of **George**

⇒ Efficiency of **Jim** = 10 − 7 = 3 units/day.

⇒ Time taken by **Jim** alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of **Jim**

⇒ Time taken by **Jim** = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task. If the ratio of time taken by A and B is x:y, then the ratio of their efficiencies is y:x.

Combined Work Rate

If person A takes 'a' days and person B takes 'b' days to complete a task individually, they will complete it together in (a × b) / (a + b) days.

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed among workers in the ratio of the total work done by each, which is the product of their individual efficiency and the time they worked.</p
